children: Indian government bonds are expected to selloff in early deals on Friday, as oil prices and U.S. Treasury yields breached key levels, reigniting inflation and rate hike concerns.
Fresh debt supply will further test investor appetite as New Delhi sells 320 billion rupees ($3.35 billion) of bonds, including a new 30-year paper.
India's benchmark 6.94% 2036 bond yield is expected to trade between 6.96% and 7.02%, a private-bank trader said, after ending the previous session at 6.9762%, a three-month high.
"Bulls have lost confidence and the benchmark yield rising above 7% seems an inevitable reality for now," the trader said.

U.S. yields climbed, with the 10-year note further extending its rise in Asian hours, after data pushed up expectations for a Federal Reserve interest rate hike next week, while soaring oil prices exacerbated inflation worries.

The 10-year U.S. yield was around 4.97%, its highest in almost three years, after data showed the U.S. producer price index increased 5.4% for 12 months through August. The bets for a 25-basis-point rate hike on Wednesday jumped to 72%, up from 62% earlier, according to the CME FedWatch tool.
Oil prices comfortably moved above the $100 per barrel mark as an escalating Middle East conflict continued to drive up global fuel costs and energy supply disruptions.

Iran-aligned Houthis seized control of Yemen's port of Mocha, posing a further threat to Red Sea traffic, while Gulf traffic remained restricted through the Strait of Hormuz amid rising tanker attacks in the region.
India is the world's third-largest oil importer and higher crude threatens to swell the import bill and stoke inflation.
Overnight indexed swap rates are set to spike, tracking Treasury yields and oil prices.
On Thursday, the one-year (INR1YMIBROIS=CC) rate ended at 6%, the two-year (INR2YMIBROIS=CC) at 6.2050% while the liquid five-year (INR5YMIBROIS=CC) rate rose 4 bps to 6.52%.
